saturationDecisions.why: at gate (2) but a changed path is on its surface

themes.theme: The e2e harness spawns a server through an npx wrapper it never truly owns: SIGTERM does not reach the real vite preview child, so the process leaks and the next run's reachability check silently attaches to a stale server instead of the one it just built.
findingSummaries: stop() sends SIGTERM to the npx wrapper, which does not forward it to the vite preview child, so the preview server outlives every run; the next run's reachable() then succeeds against that leftover server and drive.mjs reports PASS/FAIL about a build nobody just made.
themes.remediation: Bypass the npx wrapper and spawn the real vite binary directly so the process this script controls is the process actually serving; stop() then kills the thing it started, removing the indirection layer that swallows the signal instead of adding new signal-forwarding or process-group logic.

themes.theme: The responsive-layout stylesheet model the CSS guard builds from is narrower than what it claims to check — it drops out-of-order base fragments and filters positioning too tightly — so ordinary stylesheet mistakes can strand a panel while the guard stays green.
findingSummaries: placementAt concatenates the non-media tier first and the media tiers after it, and positionedSelectors only enumerates selectors that are absolute somewhere — so two ordinary stylesheet mistakes strand a panel at phone width while both assertions stay green.
themes.remediation: Remove the base-then-media reordering in placementAt so blocks are simply joined in source order, and remove the '=== absolute' restriction in positionedSelectors so it uses the single existing viewport-relative-positioning test already applicable to fixed elements — both are deletions of an overly narrow filter, not new machinery.

themes.theme: A refusal-reporting branch re-derives its answer from a validator call whose result is provably empty at that point, because an earlier branch already consumed the non-empty case — so the loud failure path the codebase relies on for priors traps is silently empty instead.
findingSummaries: The built.report.refusals.length > 0 branch answers with validateDetailed(cons, k), but line 80 already returned early when that call was non-empty — so this branch provably posts refusals: [], and the defensive path recorded in app/CLAUDE.md as the priors trap's loud failure is silent instead.
themes.remediation: Delete the re-derivation call in this branch and pass through built.report.refusals, the value the builder already computed — stop computing the same fact twice from two different code paths that can disagree.

themes.theme: The 'already optimal' toast is decided by a predicate that checks two of the quality panel's three disclosures, so a graph can fail the disclosure the toast forgot to check and still claim optimality.
findingSummaries: meetsEverySetting checks isOptimal + targetShortfall + separationShortfall, but the quality panel renders a THIRD disclosure — constraintSummary — and it is not consulted, so a graph whose buddy rules were not met (or were never checked) can still produce "That's already an optimal arrangement — a re-roll can't improve it."
themes.remediation: Extend the single existing predicate meetsEverySetting to also require zero constraint violations, and delete any separate ad hoc check at the call site — keep one predicate the toast and panel both read, rather than letting the toast maintain its own partial copy.

themes.theme: A source comment states a geometric derivation the stylesheet no longer produces, so the next reader recalibrates a breakpoint from a stale number.
findingSummaries: The comment justifying the 1360px breakpoint says "the person column starts at viewport - 594px", but #sidecol is right: calc(18px + 280px + 16px) with width: 250px, so it starts at viewport - 564px.
themes.remediation: Delete the restated arithmetic from the comment and keep only the non-obvious fact (which columns/toggle cross below this width) — the derivation duplicates values the stylesheet already holds and will go stale again the next time a width changes.

themes.theme: The roster-parser size cap bounds code points but not per-character cost, and the per-keystroke synchronous parse it is meant to make affordable has a ~40x cost spread depending on which characters fill the budget, so an attacker-chosen roster can still make every keystroke lag.
findingSummaries: MAX_PARSE_CHARS is documented as the bound that makes the on-every-keystroke re-parse affordable, but the cost per code point is not constant: it is dominated by a per-token replace under a /u regex and by clampToPoints re-walking the string whenever UTF-16 length exceeds the cap — an astral roster does this at exactly half the cap, and one keystroke measured at 5.4ms for a benign 50k-name roster versus 223ms for an astral roster of the same code-point length.
themes.remediation: Remove the per-token control-character replace (fold the hostile class into the TOKEN regex so those characters never enter a token in the first place) and remove the redundant re-walk in clampToPoints for strings already known to sit at the cap — collapse two costly passes into the single pass the cap was supposed to already bound.

themes.theme: The e2e layout harness and the CSS-completeness test each maintain their own separate, unlinked list of which panels must be checked, so #stage is present in one list and silently absent from the other with no recorded reason — and any future panel addition has to be remembered twice.
findingSummaries: responsiveCss.test.ts derives its panel list mechanically from app.css and pins it with a toEqual assertion, so a new position:absolute panel forces that test to fail until updated — but drive.mjs's PANELS array is a separate hand-typed literal with no relationship to the CSS-derived list and no completeness assertion; #stage is in the CSS-derived list but absent from PANELS, and the comment above PANELS ('every panel main renders, by the selector the stylesheet places it with') is false as written since it omits this exclusion.

#stage is checked in responsiveCss.test.ts as an absolutely-positioned element that must rejoin the flow at narrow width, but is not in the PANELS list for runtime layout verification, and the discrepancy is unexplained.
themes.remediation: Delete drive.mjs's hand-typed PANELS literal and have it import/derive the same CSS-derived selector list responsiveCss.test.ts already computes, so there is exactly one registry of checkable panels instead of two that can silently diverge.

themes.theme: Selecting a new person from within an already-open PersonPanel (via a buddy chip or Back) unmounts the focused element without redirecting focus into the new content, so the app-global focus rescue lands the user back at <main> instead of where they were reading, breaking the app's core browse-buddies keyboard workflow.
findingSummaries: PersonPanel keeps the same <section id="person"> mounted across a within-panel selection change, but its buddy/related chips and Back button are keyed by the OLD person's buddy indices, so the specific DOM node that had focus is unmounted on every hop; no code redirects focus to the new content, so App's global useFocusRescue catches it and lands focus on <main tabIndex={-1}> instead.
themes.remediation: Remove reliance on the generic global focus rescue for this in-panel case: after a within-panel selection change, move focus to the panel's own heading (already rendered, just add tabIndex={-1}) so the existing rescue mechanism is no longer the thing deciding where focus lands here.

gating.theme: the end-to-end harness does not own the lifetime of the server it claims to build, serve and drive, so it can leak a server and then silently verify a stale build
gating.summary: `stop()` sends SIGTERM to the `npx` wrapper, which does not forward it to the `vite preview` child, so the preview server outlives every run; the next run's `reachable()` then succeeds against that leftover server and `drive.mjs` reports PASS/FAIL about a build nobody just made.
gating.failure:
Reproduced twice under /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch. (1) Spawn `npx vite preview --port 4199 --strictPort` exactly as run.mjs does, wait until it answers, send `server.kill("SIGTERM")`, wait 2.5 s: `STILL SERVING AFTER SIGTERM TO npx: true`, and the server was still answering (HTTP 302 -> /ringweave/) after the parent node process had exited; `ps` showed 3 live vite processes. (2) With an unrelated HTTP server already bound to the port, run.mjs's verbatim `reachable()` loop returns true on its first iteration (it fetches BASE before the strictPort-failed vite has set `exitCode`), and the content `drive.mjs` would then drive is `

STALE BUILD

`. Concretely: run `npm run e2e`, change app source, run `npm run e2e` again -> the second run drives the first run's leaked server, so every check reports on the OLD bundle while claiming to test "the PRODUCTION BUILD ... so what is checked is what ships".
gating.remediation: Own the process group rather than the wrapper: spawn with `detached: true` and `process.kill(-server.pid, "SIGTERM")` in `stop()`, or bypass `npx` entirely and spawn `process.execPath` on `app/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js`. Close the sibling in the same change: `reachable()` must not accept a server this script did not start — check `server.exitCode !== null` *after* a failed-to-bind grace period, or have the spawned server print its ready line to stdout and gate on that, so a port already in use is a hard failure instead of a silent redirect to somebody else's build.
gating.invariant: After `scripts/e2e/run.mjs` terminates by ANY path (success, check failure, throw, SIGINT/SIGTERM), nothing is listening on `E2E_PORT`; and `drive.mjs` is only ever spawned against a server whose process this run started and still owns.

gating.theme: the responsive-layout guard states a completeness property about panels rejoining the flow that its stylesheet model does not actually deliver
gating.summary: `placementAt` concatenates the non-media tier first and the media tiers after it, and `positionedSelectors` only enumerates selectors that are `absolute` somewhere — so two ordinary stylesheet mistakes strand a panel at phone width while both assertions stay green.
gating.failure: Both reproduced with the guard's helpers copied verbatim (/home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/guard.mjs, probe1.mjs, probe4.mjs) against the real app.css. (a) Cascade order: append `#rail { position: absolute; left: 500px; }` to the END of app.css (after the `@media (max-width: 820px)` block). Browser: `@media` adds no specificity and this rule is later in source order, so `#rail` computes `absolute; left:500px` at 390px and paints at x=500..710 of a 390px viewport. Guard: `strandedPanels` returns `[]` because it evaluates `[base, 1360, 820]` in that fixed order and sees the narrow tier's `position: static` last. (b) Never-absolute panels: insert `#newpanel { position: fixed; top:14px; left:700px; width:250px }` with no entry in any media tier. Browser: off a 390px viewport at every width. Guard: `positionedSelectors` filters on `position === "absolute"`, so `#newpanel` is never enumerated — `strandedPanels` returns `[]` AND the pinned list assertion `["#buddies","#rail","#rightcol","#sidecol","#stage","#toggle"]` still passes unchanged. The docblock's claim ("a panel missing from it is the whole defect"; "enumerates them so a new one cannot be forgotten") is therefore false for both.
gating.remediation: Make `tiers()` emit blocks in source order including the base fragments that follow a media block, and have `placementAt` join them in that order rather than base-then-media. Widen `positionedSelectors` from `=== "absolute"` to "any viewport-relative positioning" (`absolute` or `fixed`), which is the property the check is actually about — a `fixed` panel carrying a viewport-edge offset is stranded for exactly the same reason. Both are subtractions from the current filters, not new machinery.
gating.invariant: For every selector S and every width W, the guard's computed placement of S equals the browser's computed `position`/inset for S at W — i.e. declarations are evaluated in stylesheet source order, and every selector the cascade ever positions out of normal flow (`absolute` OR `fixed`) is enumerated for the narrow-tier check.

gating.theme: a refusal reaching the user must carry the reason it was refused for, not a re-derivation that is guaranteed to be empty
gating.summary: The `built.report.refusals.length > 0` branch answers with `validateDetailed(cons, k)`, but line 80 already returned early when that call was non-empty — so this branch provably posts `refusals: []`, and the defensive path recorded in app/CLAUDE.md as the priors trap's loud failure is silent instead.
gating.failure: Trace: `runGeneration` computes `refusals = validateDetailed(cons, k)` at line 80 and returns `{kind:"refused"}` if non-empty. Reaching line 87 therefore implies `validateDetailed(cons, k).length === 0`. The call at line 93 is the same pure function on the same arguments, so `refusals` is always `[]`. Downstream in App.tsx:150 that yields `describeReasons([], names)[0] ?? "Those buddy rules can't all be met."` and `anyAboutARule([]) === false`, so the dialog reopens with the generic sentence and the buddy-rules disclosure stays CLOSED. The reachable trigger is the one app/CLAUDE.md names: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` validates `withHardPriors(cons)` (lib/src/core/index.ts:289) while the app validates the un-promoted `cons`, so the moment priors exist a refusal that only exists after promotion arrives with zero reasons — exactly the case this branch was written to make loud. It is also hit today by lib/src/core/index.ts:275 and :281 (roster size invalid / `n !== cons.n`), which the app's own MAX_ROSTER_N gate keeps unreachable.
gating.remediation: Do not re-derive: surface what the builder actually reported. Either re-run the validator over the same set the builder validated, or carry `built.report.refusals` through the response (widening the `refused` payload to accept prose reasons alongside structured ones) so the channel can never be empty. Guard it with the invariant below rather than with a comment.

gating.theme: the roster size cap counts characters, but the per-character cost varies ~40x with what those characters are, so a cap calibrated on plain names does not bound the synchronous per-keystroke re-parse an attacker-chosen roster forces
gating.summary: MAX_PARSE_CHARS is documented as the bound that makes the on-every-keystroke re-parse affordable ("this parse re-runs on every keystroke, so both totals are bounded here"), and RosterModal calls parseRoster synchronously inside a render-path useMemo keyed on `text`. The cap bounds CODE POINTS, but the cost per code point is not constant: it is dominated by `match[0].replace(CONTROL_CHARS, " ")` over a whole token under a /u regex, and by clampToPoints re-walking the string whenever `text.length` (UTF-16 units) exceeds the cap, which an astral roster does at exactly half the cap. Measured against the real source, one keystroke costs 5.4 ms for a benign 50k-name roster and 223 ms for a roster of the same code-point length made of astral characters — a ~40x spread entirely inside the documented budget. Nothing debounces, defers or memoizes across the keystroke, and RosterModal is the whole accessible document when it is open.
gating.failure: Drop a .txt file of 500,000 U+200B (zero-width space, BMP, exactly at MAX_PARSE_CHARS, so no truncation warning fires) onto the roster dialog, or paste 500,000 U+1F600. readFileText accepts it (well under 8 MB) and setRoster stores it. Every subsequent keystroke in the textarea then runs capText + parseRoster synchronously in render: measured 165.5 ms/keystroke for the ZWSP file and 223.5 ms/keystroke for the astral one, against 5.4 ms for an equally long roster of ordinary names (node 24, /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/dos/probeRoster.test.ts). The ZWSP roster yields ZERO names, so the entire cost buys nothing. On a phone-class device this multiplies out to roughly a second per character, which is a frozen dialog rather than jank. The guard that should have stopped it is MAX_PARSE_CHARS itself: it is enforced, it is not bypassed, and it still admits the input — because it bounds how many characters are scanned and not what scanning one costs.
gating.remediation: Bound the per-keystroke work rather than only the character count. Cheapest correct fix: hoist the control-character normalization out of the per-token `replace` and do it once over the capped text (or fold the hostile class into the TOKEN regex so those characters are non-token characters and never enter a token), and give clampToPoints a path that avoids re-walking a string already known to sit at the cap — currently the UTF-16 fast path can never fire for an astral roster, so it pays the full walk on every keystroke forever. Then add a shape-independent cost-budget test alongside the existing layout one (FORCE_MIN_TICKS has the same shape), asserting the ratio in the invariant.
gating.invariant: For every string s of at most MAX_PARSE_CHARS code points, the synchronous cost of one roster keystroke — clampToPoints(s, MAX_PARSE_CHARS) followed by parseRoster on the result — is within a fixed small constant factor (e.g. 4x) of the cost for an ASCII roster of the same code-point length. Equivalently: the number of character-level operations parseRoster and capText perform together is O(MAX_PARSE_CHARS) with a constant independent of the Unicode class and token structure of s. This is a ratio bound quantified over all admissible inputs and is property-testable over arbitrary generated Unicode strings; it is not satisfied by special-casing any particular character.

gating.theme: the e2e layout-geometry harness and the CSS-completeness test maintain two independent, unlinked lists of 'the panels that must be checked', so extending the panel set (which F9/F12/F13 will all do) does not automatically extend geometry coverage the way it automatically extends the CSS check
gating.summary: responsiveCss.test.ts derives its panel list mechanically from app.css (positionedSelectors(tiers(APP_CSS))) and pins it with a non-vacuity toEqual([...]) assertion, so a new position:absolute panel forces that test to fail until the array is updated — a seam that pays. drive.mjs's PANELS array (used by checkLayout for off-screen/overlap detection in a real browser, the check that exists specifically because #sidecol shipped off-screen at phone width) is a separate, hand-typed literal with no relationship to the CSS-derived list and no assertion that it is complete relative to it. Concretely: responsiveCss.test.ts's own positioned-selector list currently contains #stage, but drive.mjs's PANELS does not (a defensible exclusion — #stage is deliberately layered under every floating panel by design, so including it would manufacture false 'overlap' failures against #rail/#toggle/#sidecol/#buddies — but that reasoning lives nowhere: drive.mjs's comment above PANELS claims 'Every panel <main> renders, by the selector the stylesheet places it with', which is false as written since #stage is one such panel and is not in the list).
gating.failure: Add a new floating/nested panel for a real committed feature (e.g. F12's what-if result card, or F9's disruption-report disclosure, following the existing #route/#person pattern of a card inside #sidecol, or a new position:absolute panel like #route/#person's siblings) and forget to add its selector to drive.mjs's PANELS: `npm test` (responsiveCss.test.ts) only fails if the new panel is itself position:absolute in some tier and thus CSS-auto-discovered — a card nested inside #sidecol (like #route/#person today) triggers no such failure at all, since positionedSelectors only walks explicit position:absolute rules. `npm run e2e` then silently stops checking that panel's off-screen/overlap behavior at all five viewports — exactly the class of defect (`#sidecol` at x=-174 on a 390px phone) the harness was built to catch — with zero red signal anywhere in CI.
gating.remediation: Either derive PANELS in drive.mjs from the same source responsiveCss.test.ts uses (export the CSS-derived selector list, or read app.css in drive.mjs the same way and union it with the known nested-card selectors), or add a completeness assertion — e.g. a short Node script/test that fails when a DOM id present in App.tsx's rendered markup is absent from both PANELS and a documented allow-list of intentional exclusions (#stage). At minimum, correct the comment above PANELS so it states the #stage exclusion and the reason (it is deliberately layered under the floating panels), so a future contributor extending the list does not have to re-derive that reasoning from scratch or copy the gap forward.
gating.invariant: every selector id that App.tsx (or a panel it renders) exposes as a distinct floating or nested-card region reachable by a real user must appear either in scripts/e2e/drive.mjs's PANELS array or in a documented, reasoned exclusion list — no selector should be addable to the rendered UI without a mechanical prompt (test failure) to decide which bucket it goes in

gating.theme: inconsistent test coverage between static CSS tests and runtime browser tests for positioned elements
gating.summary: #stage is checked in responsiveCss.test.ts as an absolutely-positioned element that must rejoin the flow at narrow width, but is not in the PANELS list for runtime layout verification
gating.failure: PANELS list at line 50-51 is ["#rail", "#toggle", "#rightcol", "#sidecol", "#route", "#person", "#buddies", "#search", ".hint", "#metrics"], missing #stage. Yet responsiveCss.test.ts line 114 expects positionedSelectors to include ["#buddies", "#rail", "#rightcol", "#sidecol", "#stage", "#toggle"]. If #stage's CSS positioning breaks at narrow viewport (e.g., remains absolute at 820px when it should be relative), drive.mjs will not detect it even though responsiveCss.test.ts checks it statically.
gating.remediation: Either (1) add "#stage" to the PANELS list in drive.mjs line 50 to include it in runtime layout checks, or (2) add a comment explaining why #stage is deliberately excluded despite being absolutely-positioned and therefore in the responsiveCss.test.ts list. Currently the discrepancy is unexplained and could confuse future maintainers.
gating.invariant: For every selector that responsiveCss.test.ts includes in positionedSelectors (selectors positioned absolutely at any viewport tier), either (a) that selector is in the PANELS list for runtime verification, or (b) there is an explicit comment in drive.mjs explaining why it is excluded.

gating.summary: PersonPanel keeps the same <section id="person"> mounted across a within-panel selection change (App.tsx only unmounts it when `selected === null`), but its buddy/related chips and its Back button are keyed by the OLD person's buddy indices, so the specific DOM node that had focus is unmounted on every hop. No code redirects focus to the new content (e.g. the new <h2> or a control inside the panel), so App's global useFocusRescue (App.tsx:91-105) catches it by its generic contract and lands focus on <main tabIndex={-1}> instead — a valid but contextless target.

gating.remediation: After a within-panel selection change (the chip/Back paths, as distinct from a panel opening/closing), move focus explicitly to a stable element that survives the re-render — e.g. the panel's <h2> (with tabIndex={-1}) or the Close button — rather than leaving it to the app-global rescue, whose contract is 'land somewhere reachable,' not 'stay where the user was working.'
gating.invariant: For any control inside #person whose activation replaces that panel's own content while the panel itself remains mounted (a related-person chip, or Back), document.activeElement immediately after the resulting update must be contained within #person — not merely 'reachable' or 'not <body>'.

(1) Spawn `npx vite preview --port 4199 --strictPort` exactly as run.mjs does, wait until it answers, send `server.kill("SIGTERM")`, wait 2.5 s: `STILL SERVING AFTER SIGTERM TO npx: true`, and the server was still answering (HTTP 302 -> /ringweave/) after the parent node process had exited; `ps` showed 3 live vite processes. (2) With an unrelated HTTP server already bound to the port, run.mjs's verbatim `reachable()` loop returns true on its first iteration (it fetches BASE before the strictPort-failed vite has set `exitCode`), and the content `drive.mjs` would then drive is `

STALE BUILD

`. Concretely: run `npm run e2e`, change app source, run `npm run e2e` again -> the second run drives the first run's leaked server, so every check reports on the OLD bundle while claiming to test "the PRODUCTION BUILD ... so what is checked is what ships".
confirmed.remediation: Own the process group rather than the wrapper: spawn with `detached: true` and `process.kill(-server.pid, "SIGTERM")` in `stop()`, or bypass `npx` entirely and spawn `process.execPath` on `app/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js`. Close the sibling in the same change: `reachable()` must not accept a server this script did not start — check `server.exitCode !== null` *after* a failed-to-bind grace period, or have the spawned server print its ready line to stdout and gate on that, so a port already in use is a hard failure instead of a silent redirect to somebody else's build.
confirmed.invariant: After `scripts/e2e/run.mjs` terminates by ANY path (success, check failure, throw, SIGINT/SIGTERM), nothing is listening on `E2E_PORT`; and `drive.mjs` is only ever spawned against a server whose process this run started and still owns.

confirmed.theme: the responsive-layout guard states a completeness property about panels rejoining the flow that its stylesheet model does not actually deliver
confirmed.summary: `placementAt` concatenates the non-media tier first and the media tiers after it, and `positionedSelectors` only enumerates selectors that are `absolute` somewhere — so two ordinary stylesheet mistakes strand a panel at phone width while both assertions stay green.
confirmed.failure: Both reproduced with the guard's helpers copied verbatim (/home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/guard.mjs, probe1.mjs, probe4.mjs) against the real app.css. (a) Cascade order: append `#rail { position: absolute; left: 500px; }` to the END of app.css (after the `@media (max-width: 820px)` block). Browser: `@media` adds no specificity and this rule is later in source order, so `#rail` computes `absolute; left:500px` at 390px and paints at x=500..710 of a 390px viewport. Guard: `strandedPanels` returns `[]` because it evaluates `[base, 1360, 820]` in that fixed order and sees the narrow tier's `position: static` last. (b) Never-absolute panels: insert `#newpanel { position: fixed; top:14px; left:700px; width:250px }` with no entry in any media tier. Browser: off a 390px viewport at every width. Guard: `positionedSelectors` filters on `position === "absolute"`, so `#newpanel` is never enumerated — `strandedPanels` returns `[]` AND the pinned list assertion `["#buddies","#rail","#rightcol","#sidecol","#stage","#toggle"]` still passes unchanged. The docblock's claim ("a panel missing from it is the whole defect"; "enumerates them so a new one cannot be forgotten") is therefore false for both.
confirmed.remediation: Make `tiers()` emit blocks in source order including the base fragments that follow a media block, and have `placementAt` join them in that order rather than base-then-media. Widen `positionedSelectors` from `=== "absolute"` to "any viewport-relative positioning" (`absolute` or `fixed`), which is the property the check is actually about — a `fixed` panel carrying a viewport-edge offset is stranded for exactly the same reason. Both are subtractions from the current filters, not new machinery.
confirmed.invariant: For every selector S and every width W, the guard's computed placement of S equals the browser's computed `position`/inset for S at W — i.e. declarations are evaluated in stylesheet source order, and every selector the cascade ever positions out of normal flow (`absolute` OR `fixed`) is enumerated for the narrow-tier check.

confirmed.theme: a refusal reaching the user must carry the reason it was refused for, not a re-derivation that is guaranteed to be empty
confirmed.summary: The `built.report.refusals.length > 0` branch answers with `validateDetailed(cons, k)`, but line 80 already returned early when that call was non-empty — so this branch provably posts `refusals: []`, and the defensive path recorded in app/CLAUDE.md as the priors trap's loud failure is silent instead.
confirmed.failure: Trace: `runGeneration` computes `refusals = validateDetailed(cons, k)` at line 80 and returns `{kind:"refused"}` if non-empty. Reaching line 87 therefore implies `validateDetailed(cons, k).length === 0`. The call at line 93 is the same pure function on the same arguments, so `refusals` is always `[]`. Downstream in App.tsx:150 that yields `describeReasons([], names)[0] ?? "Those buddy rules can't all be met."` and `anyAboutARule([]) === false`, so the dialog reopens with the generic sentence and the buddy-rules disclosure stays CLOSED. The reachable trigger is the one app/CLAUDE.md names: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` validates `withHardPriors(cons)` (lib/src/core/index.ts:289) while the app validates the un-promoted `cons`, so the moment priors exist a refusal that only exists after promotion arrives with zero reasons — exactly the case this branch was written to make loud. It is also hit today by lib/src/core/index.ts:275 and :281 (roster size invalid / `n !== cons.n`), which the app's own MAX_ROSTER_N gate keeps unreachable.
confirmed.remediation: Do not re-derive: surface what the builder actually reported. Either re-run the validator over the same set the builder validated, or carry `built.report.refusals` through the response (widening the `refused` payload to accept prose reasons alongside structured ones) so the channel can never be empty. Guard it with the invariant below rather than with a comment.

confirmed.theme: a source comment states a geometric number the stylesheet no longer computes, so the next reader recalibrates a breakpoint from a wrong premise
confirmed.summary: The comment justifying the 1360px breakpoint says "the person column starts at `viewport - 594px`", but `#sidecol` is `right: calc(18px + 280px + 16px)` with `width: 250px`, so it starts at `viewport - 564px`.
confirmed.failure: Read the rule it describes: `#sidecol { right: calc(var(--gutter) + var(--col-w) + var(--col-gap)); width: 250px }` with `--gutter: 18px`, `--col-w: 280px`, `--col-gap: 16px` (app.css:27-29, 158). Left edge = viewport − 314 − 250 = viewport − 564, not − 594. 594 is what the arithmetic gives for `width: 280px`, i.e. the value before the column was narrowed to 250. Working the comment's own crossing equation with the true number gives 1280px, not the ~1360 it derives; the shipped breakpoint is still safe, but a reader tightening it would trust a 30px cushion that is not there.
confirmed.remediation: Either correct the figure to 564 (and the derived crossing width), or delete the arithmetic and keep only the non-obvious fact — that two card columns and a centre-anchored toggle cross below this width — since the derivation restates values the stylesheet already holds and will go stale again on the next width change.

confirmed.theme: the roster size cap counts characters, but the per-character cost varies ~40x with what those characters are, so a cap calibrated on plain names does not bound the synchronous per-keystroke re-parse an attacker-chosen roster forces
confirmed.summary: MAX_PARSE_CHARS is documented as the bound that makes the on-every-keystroke re-parse affordable ("this parse re-runs on every keystroke, so both totals are bounded here"), and RosterModal calls parseRoster synchronously inside a render-path useMemo keyed on `text`. The cap bounds CODE POINTS, but the cost per code point is not constant: it is dominated by `match[0].replace(CONTROL_CHARS, " ")` over a whole token under a /u regex, and by clampToPoints re-walking the string whenever `text.length` (UTF-16 units) exceeds the cap, which an astral roster does at exactly half the cap. Measured against the real source, one keystroke costs 5.4 ms for a benign 50k-name roster and 223 ms for a roster of the same code-point length made of astral characters — a ~40x spread entirely inside the documented budget. Nothing debounces, defers or memoizes across the keystroke, and RosterModal is the whole accessible document when it is open.
confirmed.failure: Drop a .txt file of 500,000 U+200B (zero-width space, BMP, exactly at MAX_PARSE_CHARS, so no truncation warning fires) onto the roster dialog, or paste 500,000 U+1F600. readFileText accepts it (well under 8 MB) and setRoster stores it. Every subsequent keystroke in the textarea then runs capText + parseRoster synchronously in render: measured 165.5 ms/keystroke for the ZWSP file and 223.5 ms/keystroke for the astral one, against 5.4 ms for an equally long roster of ordinary names (node 24, /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/dos/probeRoster.test.ts). The ZWSP roster yields ZERO names, so the entire cost buys nothing. On a phone-class device this multiplies out to roughly a second per character, which is a frozen dialog rather than jank. The guard that should have stopped it is MAX_PARSE_CHARS itself: it is enforced, it is not bypassed, and it still admits the input — because it bounds how many characters are scanned and not what scanning one costs.
confirmed.remediation: Bound the per-keystroke work rather than only the character count. Cheapest correct fix: hoist the control-character normalization out of the per-token `replace` and do it once over the capped text (or fold the hostile class into the TOKEN regex so those characters are non-token characters and never enter a token), and give clampToPoints a path that avoids re-walking a string already known to sit at the cap — currently the UTF-16 fast path can never fire for an astral roster, so it pays the full walk on every keystroke forever. Then add a shape-independent cost-budget test alongside the existing layout one (FORCE_MIN_TICKS has the same shape), asserting the ratio in the invariant.
confirmed.invariant: For every string s of at most MAX_PARSE_CHARS code points, the synchronous cost of one roster keystroke — clampToPoints(s, MAX_PARSE_CHARS) followed by parseRoster on the result — is within a fixed small constant factor (e.g. 4x) of the cost for an ASCII roster of the same code-point length. Equivalently: the number of character-level operations parseRoster and capText perform together is O(MAX_PARSE_CHARS) with a constant independent of the Unicode class and token structure of s. This is a ratio bound quantified over all admissible inputs and is property-testable over arbitrary generated Unicode strings; it is not satisfied by special-casing any particular character.

confirmed.theme: the e2e layout-geometry harness and the CSS-completeness test maintain two independent, unlinked lists of 'the panels that must be checked', so extending the panel set (which F9/F12/F13 will all do) does not automatically extend geometry coverage the way it automatically extends the CSS check
confirmed.summary: responsiveCss.test.ts derives its panel list mechanically from app.css (positionedSelectors(tiers(APP_CSS))) and pins it with a non-vacuity toEqual([...]) assertion, so a new position:absolute panel forces that test to fail until the array is updated — a seam that pays. drive.mjs's PANELS array (used by checkLayout for off-screen/overlap detection in a real browser, the check that exists specifically because #sidecol shipped off-screen at phone width) is a separate, hand-typed literal with no relationship to the CSS-derived list and no assertion that it is complete relative to it. Concretely: responsiveCss.test.ts's own positioned-selector list currently contains #stage, but drive.mjs's PANELS does not (a defensible exclusion — #stage is deliberately layered under every floating panel by design, so including it would manufacture false 'overlap' failures against #rail/#toggle/#sidecol/#buddies — but that reasoning lives nowhere: drive.mjs's comment above PANELS claims 'Every panel <main> renders, by the selector the stylesheet places it with', which is false as written since #stage is one such panel and is not in the list).
confirmed.failure: Add a new floating/nested panel for a real committed feature (e.g. F12's what-if result card, or F9's disruption-report disclosure, following the existing #route/#person pattern of a card inside #sidecol, or a new position:absolute panel like #route/#person's siblings) and forget to add its selector to drive.mjs's PANELS: `npm test` (responsiveCss.test.ts) only fails if the new panel is itself position:absolute in some tier and thus CSS-auto-discovered — a card nested inside #sidecol (like #route/#person today) triggers no such failure at all, since positionedSelectors only walks explicit position:absolute rules. `npm run e2e` then silently stops checking that panel's off-screen/overlap behavior at all five viewports — exactly the class of defect (`#sidecol` at x=-174 on a 390px phone) the harness was built to catch — with zero red signal anywhere in CI.
confirmed.remediation: Either derive PANELS in drive.mjs from the same source responsiveCss.test.ts uses (export the CSS-derived selector list, or read app.css in drive.mjs the same way and union it with the known nested-card selectors), or add a completeness assertion — e.g. a short Node script/test that fails when a DOM id present in App.tsx's rendered markup is absent from both PANELS and a documented allow-list of intentional exclusions (#stage). At minimum, correct the comment above PANELS so it states the #stage exclusion and the reason (it is deliberately layered under the floating panels), so a future contributor extending the list does not have to re-derive that reasoning from scratch or copy the gap forward.
confirmed.invariant: every selector id that App.tsx (or a panel it renders) exposes as a distinct floating or nested-card region reachable by a real user must appear either in scripts/e2e/drive.mjs's PANELS array or in a documented, reasoned exclusion list — no selector should be addable to the rendered UI without a mechanical prompt (test failure) to decide which bucket it goes in

confirmed.theme: inconsistent test coverage between static CSS tests and runtime browser tests for positioned elements
confirmed.summary: #stage is checked in responsiveCss.test.ts as an absolutely-positioned element that must rejoin the flow at narrow width, but is not in the PANELS list for runtime layout verification
confirmed.failure: PANELS list at line 50-51 is ["#rail", "#toggle", "#rightcol", "#sidecol", "#route", "#person", "#buddies", "#search", ".hint", "#metrics"], missing #stage. Yet responsiveCss.test.ts line 114 expects positionedSelectors to include ["#buddies", "#rail", "#rightcol", "#sidecol", "#stage", "#toggle"]. If #stage's CSS positioning breaks at narrow viewport (e.g., remains absolute at 820px when it should be relative), drive.mjs will not detect it even though responsiveCss.test.ts checks it statically.
confirmed.remediation: Either (1) add "#stage" to the PANELS list in drive.mjs line 50 to include it in runtime layout checks, or (2) add a comment explaining why #stage is deliberately excluded despite being absolutely-positioned and therefore in the responsiveCss.test.ts list. Currently the discrepancy is unexplained and could confuse future maintainers.
confirmed.invariant: For every selector that responsiveCss.test.ts includes in positionedSelectors (selectors positioned absolutely at any viewport tier), either (a) that selector is in the PANELS list for runtime verification, or (b) there is an explicit comment in drive.mjs explaining why it is excluded.

confirmed.theme: Selecting a new person from *within* the already-open PersonPanel (a buddy/related-person chip, or Back) does not keep focus inside that panel; it resets to the page's <main> landmark, so a keyboard/screen-reader user doing the app's core 'find someone, then browse who their buddies are' workflow loses their place after every hop and has to Tab from the very top of the document (through the reroll/edit-people buttons, the layout toggle, etc.) to get back into the panel they were just reading.
confirmed.summary: PersonPanel keeps the same <section id="person"> mounted across a within-panel selection change (App.tsx only unmounts it when `selected === null`), but its buddy/related chips and its Back button are keyed by the OLD person's buddy indices, so the specific DOM node that had focus is unmounted on every hop. No code redirects focus to the new content (e.g. the new <h2> or a control inside the panel), so App's global useFocusRescue (App.tsx:91-105) catches it by its generic contract and lands focus on <main tabIndex={-1}> instead — a valid but contextless target.
confirmed.failure: Reproduced with an 8-person roster: select Alice (BuddyList row), focus her first buddy chip ("Bob"), press Enter/click it. document.activeElement becomes the <main> element (its full textContent spans the whole app UI) rather than anything inside #person. Same result clicking "← Back" after a hop. scripts/e2e/drive.mjs exercises this exact sequence (lines 270-277, "every name in the panel is clickable") but only asserts the new h2 text, never where focus lands, so the gap is untested end to end as well as in the unit suite.
confirmed.remediation: After a within-panel selection change (the chip/Back paths, as distinct from a panel opening/closing), move focus explicitly to a stable element that survives the re-render — e.g. the panel's <h2> (with tabIndex={-1}) or the Close button — rather than leaving it to the app-global rescue, whose contract is 'land somewhere reachable,' not 'stay where the user was working.'
confirmed.invariant: For any control inside #person whose activation replaces that panel's own content while the panel itself remains mounted (a related-person chip, or Back), document.activeElement immediately after the resulting update must be contained within #person — not merely 'reachable' or 'not <body>'.

plausible.theme: the 'already optimal' toast must be false whenever the quality panel is still disclosing something the graph did not deliver
plausible.summary: `meetsEverySetting` checks `isOptimal` + `targetShortfall` + `separationShortfall`, but the quality panel renders a THIRD disclosure — `constraintSummary` — and it is not consulted, so a graph whose buddy rules were not met (or were never checked) can still produce "That's already an optimal arrangement — a re-roll can't improve it."
plausible.failure: `QualityPanel.tsx:64` renders `constraintSummary(view)` as a `.rules-line` alongside the two shortfall lines. `constraintSummary` returns `"N of M buddy rules couldn't be met"` when `report.reqViolations + report.prohViolations > 0`, and `"N buddy rules saved with this graph — not re-checked on import."` when `report === null` with rules present (every imported constrained graph). `meetsEverySetting` reads neither. Note `separationShortfall` returns null whenever `constraints.length > 0`, so for a constrained view the predicate collapses to `isOptimal && targetShortfall === null` — nothing in it is about the rules at all. I could not reach the violation case from the app: 15,600 randomized constrained builds (n 5..14, k 2..5, /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/probe3.mjs) produced zero reports with `refusals.length === 0 && reqViolations + prohViolations > 0`, so today this rests on the core continuing to place every required edge and no prohibited one — hence PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED. This is the literal sibling of the defect the comment at App.tsx:37-41 records as already fixed once ("'Optimal' has to mean every disclosure the quality panel is making is clear, not just the buddy count").
plausible.remediation: Fold the rules disclosure into the same predicate: `meetsEverySetting` should additionally require `view.report !== null ? view.report.reqViolations + view.report.prohViolations === 0 : view.constraints.length === 0`. Keeping the panel and the toast on one predicate is what the function already exists for; extend it rather than adding a second test at the App.tsx call site.
plausible.invariant: `meetsEverySetting(v) === true` implies the quality panel renders no unmet-expectation line for `v` — i.e. `targetShortfall(v) === null && separationShortfall(v) === null && (v.constraints.length === 0 || (v.report !== null && v.report.reqViolations + v.report.prohViolations === 0))`.
